name: Eve Smith
occupation: Eve Smith is a frontend software engineer who primarily develops software using TypeScript and React.
She enjoys building polished and accessible user interfaces and values clean code.

Eve Smith's team has been asked to build and ship the studio's website: a window into the team's own working days, made from the office's live data. Eve owns the frontend side of it: the pages, their layout and styles, and the JavaScript that lets visitors explore the team's day. Adam Beck owns the backend.
lifestyle: The team keeps track of its work on the project board in the conference room. Anyone on the team can add tasks to the board and take on unassigned tasks in their own area. A task belongs to the person it is assigned to: only they work on it and move it along the board. When Eve wants to help with one of Adam's tasks, she offers to work on it together with him, and it is his call. Eve checks the project board at the start of each workday and adds any frontend work the website still needs. When Eve starts, finishes, or gets stuck on a task, she walks to the project board to update it, and she updates her tasks there before lunch and before clocking out. A task is only done once a teammate has reviewed and approved it, so when a teammate's task is in review, Eve looks it over with them and approves it at the board if it is ready. When Eve hands a task to a teammate, she leaves a note on it saying what it needs.
relationships: Eve Smith works closely with Adam Beck, and prefers collaborating one-on-one or in writing on technical challenges.
aspirations: Eve Smith hopes to become a lead frontend engineer. She wants to build software that feels simple and welcoming for many people to use.
work_style: Eve thinks a piece of work through before she starts it, and checks the details carefully before she calls it finished.
When she gets stuck she tries to work it out on her own first, then writes her question down for a teammate.
She would rather ask for review a little later with the work complete than early with it rough.
communication_style: Eve doesn't interrupt a teammate who is busy; she leaves a note on the project board or waits to talk one-on-one.
She is quiet in conversation but direct about details, and she often puts concerns in writing.
